answer: To resist sybils, agents must harvest nectar from timber-lined terraces only after proving continuous physical presence via timed sensor logs. Each identity requires depositing a unique timber sample whose growth rings encode a private key, then confirming the terrace coordinates match the nectar yield signature. Attackers cloning identities incur high costs shipping and aging real timber pieces across many terraces while faking the biological nectar production rates that cannot be simulated cheaply at scale.
